cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities where error pages incorporate user-controllable data (error messages, stack traces, query parameters) into HTML responses without proper output encoding, leading to cross-site scripting or information disclosure, as well as a memory exhaustion issue from unbounded caching of attacker-influenced error pages.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Generate a random error code, set it as request attribute, and modify the JSP to output only the error code instead of the exception details. Log the exception server-side..

mechanism.typical_fix: Generate a random error code, set it as request attribute, and modify the JSP to output only the error code instead of the exception details. Log the exception server-side.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Generate a random error code, set it as request attribute, and modify the JSP to output only the error code instead of the exception details. Log the exception server-side.
sub_patterns.name: Full exception stack trace disclosure in error response
sub_patterns.root_cause: The error page retrieves the exception from the request attribute and prints its full stack trace to the HTML output without sanitization, assuming full error details are safe for end users.
